# Estimating loss from a steady balance

At steady state, accumulation is zero, so input equals useful output plus loss.
Subtract the useful output from the input to estimate the loss.

For an input of 100 W and a useful output of 80 W, the balance gives
100 W = 80 W + loss. Subtracting 80 W from both sides gives a loss of
20 W, or 20% of the input.

The estimate means one fifth of the input is not delivered as useful output;
it can be compared with another design measured over the same boundary.
This balance assumes steady operation and accounts for all flows across that
boundary. During warm-up, stored energy changes, so the difference alone does
not establish the loss.

A changed assumption may invalidate the interpretation above.
